title: Meetings & Events Service Charge Rates and Sales Tax Treatment
content:
The service charge on a Meetings & Events event bill is a percentage of food and beverage revenue that varies by package, and the package also settles whether that service charge bears sales tax, whether it reaches room rental, and how a food and beverage minimum shortfall is treated for service charge and sales tax.

| Package | Service charge on food and beverage revenue | Service charge bears sales tax | Service charge applies to room rental | Minimum shortfall bears service charge | Minimum shortfall bears sales tax |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Executive Boardroom Package | 22 percent | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Half-Day Meeting Package | 22 percent | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Full-Day Meeting Package | 22 percent | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Social Reception Package | 24 percent | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Wedding Celebration Package | 25 percent | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Conference Plenary Package | 23 percent | Yes | No | No | Yes |

## The same settings, read across all packages

- The service charge never applies to room rental under any Meetings & Events package.
- The service charge itself bears sales tax under every package.
- A food and beverage minimum shortfall bears no service charge under any package, and bears sales tax under every package.
- Only the service charge rate differs between packages: 22 percent for the Executive Boardroom, Half-Day Meeting and Full-Day Meeting packages, 23 percent for the Conference Plenary Package, 24 percent for the Social Reception Package and 25 percent for the Wedding Celebration Package.

The sales tax rate is the one recorded on the individual event contract; it is not set by the package.

## Hypothetical illustration

On a Social Reception Package bill with food and beverage revenue of 6,000.00, the service charge is 24 percent of 6,000.00, that is 1,440.00. The 1,440.00 bears sales tax at the contract's rate. Had the same bill carried room rental, the rental would not have borne the 24 percent.
